summary:
The Linux-specific part of this area is only in src/core/midi.c and the two tests. midi.c uses libasound: a blocking listing client, and per input a non-blocking client named "RadioS" with a write-only port subscribed to the device. Each input also subscribes to the system announce port 0:1, runs a reader thread on poll() with a self-pipe, re-checks its subscription every second, and decodes NOTEON/NOTEOFF, CONTROLLER and PITCHBEND sequencer events.

Most of midi.c is already platform-neutral and stays verbatim: mapping keys and labels, the Listener/Delivery ref-counting, delivery to the GMainContext through G_PRIORITY_HIGH_IDLE idle sources, and lost-exactly-once. src/ui/midi_ui.c needs no functional change: device follow, GTask list/open jobs, the lost-input "watch" that keeps listening for new ports, the 5 s retry, "Yenile", learn mode, the verify dialog and action dispatch all sit on the public contract. Only the SDBASE midi_mapping document is persisted; it stores the device display name and keys like "cc:1:7", never the ALSA client:port id. So nothing in SDBASE changes, but device names saved on Linux will not match Windows names and the operator re-selects the device once.

Recommended Windows design:
- midi.c becomes common code that includes exactly one backend, midi_alsa.c (today's code moved unchanged) or midi_winmm.c, chosen by G_OS_WIN32; the public API stays identical plus an additive radios_midi_decode_message().
- WinMM midiIn with CALLBACK_FUNCTION; the callback only pushes into a CRITICAL_SECTION ring and calls SetEvent. A per-input worker waits with WaitForMultipleObjects on stop/data/hotplug events with a 1 s timeout, decodes, and delivers through the existing queue(). CALLBACK_EVENT is not a valid mode for MIDI input.
- Hotplug: a per-input CM_Register_Notification (device interfaces, all classes). A removal whose link matches the device-interface path from midiInMessage(DRV_QUERYDEVICEINTERFACE), or a driver MIM_CLOSE, means LOST at once. An arrival triggers a burst of WinMM list rescans, and PORT is emitted from the list difference. A 1 s stale-handle and presence check is the fallback.
- On LOST the HMIDIIN is released immediately, because classic WinMM input is exclusive per device; the input keeps watching and reporting PORT until closed.
- The persisted identity stays the display name: WinMM szPname read through the W API, with " #N" added only for exact duplicates, ordered by interface path. The transient id is "index:fnv32", re-verified at open so an index shift never opens the wrong device.
- Tests: /midi/keys stays portable and a new /midi/decode is added. /midi/virtual-controller on Windows runs only against a loopback port named in an environment variable, otherwise it is skipped; it never opens real hardware. The fake-ALSA hotplug test gets a Windows twin built on an injectable WinMM/CfgMgr function table, with new cases for driver close, SysEx, index shift, duplicate names and same-socket replug. The Xvfb GUI runner returns 77 on Windows, so the ui-* cases need a Windows runner from the test-infra area.
files_touched: src/core/midi.c (split into common code that includes one backend; adds radios_midi_decode_message; optionally a public error quark/enum)
src/core/midi_alsa.c (new: current ALSA list/open/reader/announcement/subscribed/translate/close moved unchanged; not a separate translation unit)
include/radios/midi.h (comment updates; additive radios_midi_decode_message; optional RADIOS_MIDI_ERROR enum with a BUSY code)
src/ui/midi_ui.c (no functional change required; recommended: busy status text, *.JSON filter, comment wording)
tests/test_midi.c (guard ALSA code; new /midi/decode; Windows loopback version of /midi/virtual-controller)
tests/test_midi_hotplug.c (unchanged on Linux, or refactored to share scenarios)
CMakeLists.txt (line 19 ALSA pkg-config only when not WIN32; lines 93-94 link winmm/cfgmgr32 on WIN32; lines 191-208 test targets/registration)
docs (Windows MIDI operator notes; midi.h wording)
key_decisions: Public API in midi.h stays identical. Additive only: radios_midi_decode_message() and, recommended, a public error enum with a BUSY code. The ALSA backend is kept for Linux.

Backend is chosen at compile time with G_OS_WIN32. midi.c holds the common code and #includes midi_alsa.c or midi_winmm.c, so tests that #include midi.c keep working. Both backend structs must use the field names listener, context, alive and port_id.

WinMM midiIn uses CALLBACK_FUNCTION. The callback does only a critical-section ring push and SetEvent (no multimedia or GLib calls). One worker thread per input, using WaitForMultipleObjects with a 1 s timeout, decodes and calls the existing queue() to the GMainContext. CALLBACK_EVENT is not valid for MIDI input; CALLBACK_THREAD is an acceptable alternative.

Hotplug: per-input CM_Register_Notification on device interfaces of all classes. A removal matching the input's device-interface path (from DRV_QUERYDEVICEINTERFACE, compared case-insensitively or by device instance), or a driver MIM_CLOSE, means immediate LOST.

PORT is emitted only from WinMM device-list differences: a burst of rescans every 250 ms for 3 s after a PnP arrival, plus a 1 s periodic rescan. It is never emitted directly from the PnP event, because WinMM's list lags PnP.

Liveness fallback: a stale-handle query (midiInGetDevCapsW on the handle, midiInGetID) or two consecutive scans without the input's identity. Device indexes are never compared, because they shift when other devices are removed.

On LOST the HMIDIIN is released at once, because classic WinMM input is exclusive per device; the input keeps running as the 'watch' that reports PORT. Close order: stop flag, SetEvent, join, stop/reset/unprepare/close, CM_Unregister_Notification, CloseHandle.

The persisted identity remains the display name: szPname read with the W API and converted UTF-16 to UTF-8; exact duplicates get ' #N', ordered by interface path. The transient id is 'index:fnv32hex', re-resolved by fingerprint at open.

SysEx: 4 x 1 KiB buffers re-queued by the worker (never in the callback); content ignored, the same as ALSA. Realtime messages (clock 0xF8, active sensing 0xFE), program change and aftertouch are filtered in the callback.

Tests never open real devices implicitly (exclusive access could take a live controller from a running RadioS). The Windows hotplug test injects a fake RadioSMidiWinApi through the RADIOS_MIDI_WIN_API macro, so no midiIn*/CM_* symbols are imported (checked with objdump). Real WinMM is tested only through a loopback port named in an environment variable.
risks: R1: what WinMM does when an open device is pulled out is undocumented and driver-dependent: whether MIM_CLOSE arrives and whether queries on the stale handle fail. Without PnP notifications, a replug in the same socket faster than 1 s may go unnoticed. Needs testing on real hardware (classic usbaudio, vendor drivers, Windows MIDI Services).
R2: WinMM's device list lags PnP arrival by an unknown time. The rescan burst should keep reconnect under 1.2 s; verify on hardware.

R3: classic WinMM input is exclusive. A device held by another application (DAW, editor) or by a second RadioS fails with MMSYSERR_ALLOCATED and shows the misleading 'takılı değil' unless the busy-status UI change is adopted.

R4: device names change between platforms and setups: 31-character truncation, the classic '2- ' prefix assigned in plug order, Windows MIDI Services naming modes and custom names, and Linux ALSA names imported through transfer packages. The operator must re-select the device; bindings are kept.

R5: radios_midi_input_close runs on the GTK thread and joins the worker. If the worker is inside a slow WinMM enumeration (first Windows MIDI Services call, USB storm), the UI can stall for that call. Mitigation: rescans check the stop flag between devices; a detached teardown is the fallback.
R6: under Windows MIDI Services, WinMM is backed by the midisrv service. First-call latency and possible COM requirements in GTask threads are unknown; CoInitializeEx in the worker is the fallback.
R7: all-interface-class notifications bring many unrelated events. They are cheap and coalesced, but could be narrowed after verification.
R8: Windows timer granularity (~15.6 ms) and G_DEBUG=fatal-warnings in tests: device names must be sanitized to valid UTF-8, and expected failures logged with g_debug, never g_warning.
R9: without a Windows GUI runner, every ui-* hotplug case silently skips with exit code 77, because the current runner needs Xvfb.
R10: refactoring the Linux hotplug test to share scenarios must keep its assertions exactly; otherwise duplicate the test bodies for Windows.
cross_area_dependencies: Build/toolchain: in CMakeLists.txt line 19, call pkg_check_modules(ALSA) only when not WIN32 (MSYS2 has no alsa.pc); link winmm and cfgmgr32 on WIN32; define _WIN32_WINNT=0x0A00 and WINVER=0x0A00 globally (cfgmgr32.h needs at least 0x0602 to declare CM_Register_Notification); keep MinGW headers as system includes under -Wpedantic -Werror.

Test infrastructure: a Windows GUI test runner to replace tests/run_rotation_editor_regressions.py, which needs Xvfb and GDK_BACKEND=x11 and returns 77 on Windows; set G_DEBUG=fatal-warnings and put the GTK DLL directory on PATH through the CTest ENVIRONMENT property; confirm the MSYS2 GLib returns 77 when every test case is skipped.
Audio/preferences area: src/ui/preferences.c:330-359 hardware_max_rate() reads /proc/asound and needs a WASAPI/MMDevice replacement. It is not MIDI, but was found during the ALSA scan.
SDBASE: no change (the midi_mapping validator in desktop_api.py:42-69 is platform-neutral). Documented behaviour: device names imported from Linux will not match Windows names.

Docs/l10n: Windows operator notes (exclusive access, re-selecting the device after migration or MIDI Services renaming, duplicate-name suffix) and the new Turkish error and status strings listed in spec sections 3.10 and 3.12.
Packaging: nothing to bundle for MIDI; winmm.dll and cfgmgr32.dll are system DLLs.
platform_api_needs: None required from include/radios/platform.h. MIDI calls WinMM (winmm) and CfgMgr32 (cfgmgr32) directly through its own injectable table in src/core/midi_winmm_api.h, plus GLib's g_utf16_to_utf8, g_utf8_make_valid, g_utf8_casefold and g_win32_error_message(GetLastError()).

Build-wide defines: -D_WIN32_WINNT=0x0A00 -DWINVER=0x0A00 (at least 0x0602 is needed for the CM_Register_Notification and CM_Unregister_Notification declarations in mingw cfgmgr32.h). The UTF-8 manifest is not relied on, because only W APIs are used.

OPTIONAL, only if the platform team centralizes PnP watching: RadioSPlatformDeviceWatch *radios_platform_device_watch_new(const GUID *interface_class_or_NULL /* NULL = all interface classes */, void (*callback)(gboolean arrived, const gchar *symbolic_link_casefolded_utf8, gpointer user), gpointer user). The callback runs on a system thread-pool thread and may fire before _new returns. void radios_platform_device_watch_free(RadioSPlatformDeviceWatch *watch) blocks until running callbacks finish and must not be called from inside a callback. MIDI would call it through RadioSMidiWinApi so tests can still fake it.
